title: introduce-invocation-topology-traces-and-cost-mosaic-writer
author: Jamal Ortiz
description:
Context: We currently emit token-level traces and basic invocation spans but lack a way to see invocation topology (call/child relationships across microservices and runtime stages) coupled with a lightweight cost mosaic that surfaces expensive invocation segments. This makes SLO triage and cost debugging for multi-stage requests slow (ENG-3210).

Motivation: Provide engineers and SREs an end-to-end investigatory surface that links: 1) per-invocation topology (entry -> kernel queue -> runtime -> kv-cache -> fallback), 2) sampled token phase timing, and 3) a compact cost 'mosaic' view that highlights which stage(s) contributed most to token/unit cost. This PR introduces a topology tracing library, a mosaic writer that aggregates cost slices for dashboards, and a companion dashboard JSON and docs.

What changed (high level): Adds a topology tracer that synthesizes parent/child relationships from existing span IDs and lightweight edge heuristics; introduces a token-phase snapshot event that attaches phase timings to invocation spans; adds a cost-mosaic writer that reduces per-invocation token cost into 5 buckets and emits rollup documents for dashboards; includes a Grafana dashboard JSON for the mosaic and a docs page with rollout and troubleshooting steps.

Design notes: - Topology tracer attaches a deterministic topology_key to each span derived from (service, stage, kernel_hint). It does not change the public trace IDs. - Snapshot events are sampled 1% by default with a configurable per-tenant multiplier (config key: observability.snapshot_rate). - Cost mosaic aggregates per-invocation tokens into buckets: compute, kv-cache, kernel-queue, network, misc. Buckets are derived from existing token attribution tags; where missing, we fall back to phase-duration heuristics. - Writer is implemented as an async, bounded worker to avoid applying backpressure to critical request paths. Backpressure is mitigated by a small token buffer and drop-policy metrics exposed as observability:observability.mosaic_drop_count.

Checklist: 
- [x] Topology tracer library (src/observability/topology_tracer.go)
- [x] Token-phase snapshot event (pkg/telemetry/snapshot.go)
- [x] Cost mosaic writer (services/mosaic/writer.go)
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/cost-mosaic.json)
- [x] Docs and runbook (docs/observability/cost-mosaic.md)
- [x] Unit + integration tests (perf/bench/invocation_sampler_test.go, pkg/telemetry/snapshot_test.go)
- [x] Load-tested write path (benchmarks/mosaic_write_bench.md)

Backwards compatibility and rollout: Default sampling is low (1%) and feature gated via config and feature flags. No trace ID or span schema breaking changes. The writer will start in 'dry-run' mode in the rollout plan for 24h to validate telemetry volumes; after that we enable persisted rollups. See docs/observability/cost-mosaic.md for the toggle and runbook.

Benchmarks: On a 32-GPU staging cluster with representative workload: - Mosaic writer avg CPU overhead per 1k invocations: +0.07 CPU-seconds - Median added p99 latency on hotpath (measured at service ingress): +1.4ms (within SLO) - Observed mosaic payloads: ~34KB per 1k sampled invocations (rollup compressed to ~10KB before storage) - With default sampling (1%), storage estimate: ~2.5GB/day for a mid-tier customer (guidance in docs).

Commit summary: 
- 8b3f2c2: add topology tracer and unit tests
- d1a9e77: implement token-phase snapshot events, add serialization layer
- 5f4b0a1: cost mosaic writer and async worker, add drop metrics
- 3a7c11f: add Grafana dashboard and dashboard generator tooling
- 9d2e4b3: docs and runbook; add feature flag and config knobs

Files changed (representative): 
- src/observability/topology_tracer.go
- pkg/telemetry/snapshot.go
- services/mosaic/writer.go
- services/mosaic/worker_pool.go
- dashboards/cost-mosaic.json
- docs/observability/cost-mosaic.md
- pkg/telemetry/serializer.go
- perf/bench/invocation_sampler_test.go
- tests/integration/mosaic_integration_test.go

Testing and CI: Unit tests and integration tests run in CI. Initial CI run had a flaky test (perf/bench/invocation_sampler_test.go) due to timing, fixed by replacing wall-clock dependency with a fake clock. All checks passed on the final run (lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke).

Migration: No DB schema changes. Rollup storage uses an existing compressed blob table (mosaic_rollups) with a new jsonschema version header for graceful migration. We increment schema_version in the writer to 3.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge to main with feature flag off.
2) Enable dry-run (emits rollup to internal sink only) for 24 hours, monitor observability.mosaic_drop_count and writer queue depth.
3) Turn on persisted rollups for 5% traffic for 48 hours.
4) Ramp sampling/config to 1% tenant default.
5) Open dashboard to SREs and run RCA playbook for 7 days.

Related: ENG-3210 (cost-mosaic), ENG-3301 (topology tracing).

review_comments: Asha Patel (2025-11-22): Nice end-to-end. A couple asks: please add a metric for writer queue latency distribution and expose the default snapshot rate as a gauge. Also prefer a smaller default buffer for the worker pool (you had 10k queued tokens).

Jamal Ortiz (2025-11-23): Addressed — added writer.queue_latency_histogram and observability.snapshot_rate_gauge. Reduced default buffer to 2k and made it an env-configurable value. Added notes in docs explaining tradeoffs.
Luca Moretti (2025-11-25): Can you justify the phase-bucket heuristics when attribution tags are missing? I worry about noisy attribution leading to misleading mosaics.

Jamal Ortiz (2025-11-25): Added fallback confidence score with the rollup. Mosaic now includes a confidence float per bucket and the dashboard highlights low-confidence rollups. Also added a sampling knob to force higher confidence on a small proportion of invocations to validate heuristics.
Renee Kim (2025-11-28): Tests look good. Please add a short snippet in docs showing how to query mosaics for a given tenant and timeframe. Also, can we add an alert to watch mosaic_drop_count?
Jamal Ortiz (2025-11-28): Added query examples to docs and a recommended alert rule (SLO: if mosaic_drop_count > 100/min then pager). Updated dashboard description with link to runbook.
release_notes: Add invocation topology tracing and a cost mosaic rollup writer. Default sampling off; feature gated. Provides a Grafana dashboard and runbook to accelerate SLO triage and token-cost debugging.
notes: Feature is behind config and default sampling is conservative. SRE to monitor mosaic_drop_count and writer.queue_length during ramp.
performance_summary: Median added latency: +1.4ms; CPU overhead: +0.07 CPU-s / 1k invocations; storage estimate: ~2.5GB/day at 1% sample for mid-tier customer.
